All graphs are finite, simple, and undirected. Cycles are considered as subgraphs, not necessarily induced subgraphs. A graph homomorphism from \(G\) to \(H\) is a map \(f:V(G)\to V(H)\) such that \(f(u)f(v)\in E(H)\) whenever \(uv\in E(G)\); the map need not be injective.

For a real number \(c\in[0,1]\), consider the following property: there exists a finite graph \(H_c\) containing no cycle of length \(3\) such that, for every integer \(n\geq1\), every graph \(G\) on \(n\) vertices containing no cycle of length \(3\) or \(5\), and in which every vertex has at least \(cn\) neighbors, admits a homomorphism to \(H_c\). The graph \(H_c\) may depend on \(c\), but not on \(n\) or \(G\).

What is the exact infimum of the numbers \(c\in[0,1]\) having this property?
</problem>

9	* for every \(c>1/9\), the required finite triangle-free target exists;

14	I give both proofs. The only general theorems used are the degree form of Szemerédi’s regularity lemma and the Borsuk–Ulam theorem. All the consequences specific to this problem are proved below. The Python at the end performs exact, nontrivial checks of the constructions and the finite combinatorial parts of the proof.
15	
16	## 1. Preliminaries
17	
18	Write \(N_J(S)=\bigcup_{v\in S}N_J(v)\).
19	
20	We will repeatedly use the following elementary fact:
21	
22	> A simple graph has an odd closed walk of length at most five if and only if it contains a \(C_3\) or a \(C_5\).
23	
24	Indeed, a shortest odd closed subwalk of an odd closed walk is an odd cycle.
25	
26	Here is another useful observation.
27	
28	### Extension lemma
29	
30	Suppose \(I\subseteq V(G)\), both \(I\) and \(N_G(I)\) are independent, and \(G-I\) maps to a triangle-free graph on \(h\) vertices. Then \(G\) maps to a triangle-free graph on at most \(2h+1\) vertices.
31	
32	**Proof.** Let \(f:G-I\to H\). Replace every vertex \(a\in V(H)\) by two vertices \((a,0),(a,1)\). Put an edge between \((a,b)\) and \((a',b')\) when \(aa'\in E(H)\), except that edges with \(b=b'=1\) are omitted. Add a new vertex adjacent to all the \(1\)-copies.
33	
34	The resulting graph is triangle-free: triangles not using the new vertex would project to triangles in \(H\), and the new vertex has an independent neighborhood.
35	
36	Map \(x\in G-I\) to
37	\[
38	\bigl(f(x),\mathbf1_{x\in N_G(I)}\bigr),
39	\]
40	and map all of \(I\) to the new vertex. This is a homomorphism. ∎
41	
42	## 2. A regularity support lemma
43	
44	This is the regularity consequence needed for the upper bound.
45	
46	### Support lemma
47	
48	Fix \(0<q<c\). There are constants \(M,n_0\) such that every \(\{C_3,C_5\}\)-free graph \(G\) with
49	\[
50	n\ge n_0,\qquad \delta(G)\ge cn
51	\]
52	has the following objects:
53	
54	* disjoint sets \(V_1,\ldots,V_m\), each of size \(L\), where \(m\le M\);
55	* a graph \(R\) on \([m]\), with \(\delta(R)\ge qm\);
56	* for every \(v\in V(G)\), a set \(S_v\subseteq[m]\);
57	
58	satisfying:
59	
60	1. \(v\) has at least \(qmL\) neighbors in \(\bigcup_{i\in S_v}V_i\);
61	2. \(S_v\) is independent in \(R\);
62	3. if \(vw\in E(G)\), then
63	   \[
64	   N_R(S_v)\cap N_R(S_w)=\varnothing;
65	   \]
66	4. if \(v,x,w\) is a two-edge path in \(G\), then there are no \(R\)-edges between \(S_v\) and \(S_w\).
67	
68	**Proof.** Choose positive constants
69	\[
70	\varepsilon\ll d,\rho\ll c-q.
71	\]
72	Apply degree-form regularity. Thus there is an exceptional set \(V_0\), of size at most \(\varepsilon n\), and equal-sized clusters \(V_1,\ldots,V_m\), such that the reduced graph \(R\) consists of \(\varepsilon\)-regular pairs of density at least \(d\), and
73	\[
74	\delta(R)\ge(c-d-2\varepsilon)m\ge qm.
75	\]
76	
77	Define
78	\[
79	S_v=\{i:|N_G(v)\cap V_i|\ge \rho L\}.
80	\]
81	The neighbors not counted in these support clusters number at most
82	\[
83	|V_0|+\rho mL.
84	\]
85	Consequently, by our choice of constants,
86	\[
87	\left|N_G(v)\cap\bigcup_{i\in S_v}V_i\right|
88	 \ge cn-|V_0|-\rho mL\ge qmL.
89	\]
90	
91	We verify the remaining assertions. The elementary regular-pair facts used here are:
92	
93	* two subsets of size at least \(\rho L\) in a regular pair contain an edge;
94	* given such a subset \(A\) in one cluster of a regular pair, all but \(\varepsilon L\) vertices of the other cluster have many neighbors in \(A\).
95	
96	These follow immediately from the definition of regularity, since \(\varepsilon\ll d,\rho\). Taking \(n_0\) large lets us avoid any fixed collection of already specified vertices.
97	
98	If \(ij\in E(R)\) with \(i,j\in S_v\), an edge between the corresponding subsets of \(N_G(v)\) gives a triangle. Thus \(S_v\) is independent.
99	
100	Suppose \(vw\in E(G)\), and a cluster \(t\) belongs to both \(N_R(S_v)\) and \(N_R(S_w)\). Choose
101	\[
102	i\in S_v,\quad j\in S_w,\quad it,jt\in E(R).
103	\]
104	Regularity supplies distinct vertices
105	\[
106	a\in N_G(v)\cap V_i,\quad b\in V_t,\quad
107	a'\in N_G(w)\cap V_j
108	\]
109	with \(ab,ba'\in E(G)\), avoiding \(v,w\). This also works when \(i=j\). Then
110	\[
111	v,a,b,a',w,v
112	\]
113	is a \(C_5\), a contradiction.
114	
115	Finally, suppose \(v,x,w\) is a two-edge path and \(ij\in E(R)\), where \(i\in S_v\) and \(j\in S_w\). An edge
116	\[
117	ab,\qquad a\in N_G(v)\cap V_i,\quad b\in N_G(w)\cap V_j,
118	\]
119	chosen to avoid \(v,x,w\), gives the \(C_5\)
120	\[
121	v,x,w,b,a,v.
122	\]
123	This proves the lemma. ∎
124	
125	## 3. Upper bound: every \(c>1/9\) works
126	
127	Fix
128	\[
129	\frac19<q<c
130	\]
131	and apply the support lemma.
132	
133	Partition the vertices according to their support \(S_v\). There are at most \(2^M\) classes.
134	
135	Call a support class **small** if its support \(S\) satisfies
136	\[
137	|S|<2qm.
138	\]
139	
140	### Small classes can be removed and later restored
141	
142	If \(u,v\) belong to the same small class, each has at least \(qmL\) neighbors in a set of size less than \(2qmL\). Thus \(u,v\) have a common neighbor.
143	
144	It follows that the class \(I\) is independent: an edge within it would give a triangle.
145	
146	Moreover, there cannot be a three-edge walk from one vertex of \(I\) to another. Combining that walk with a common neighbor would give an odd closed walk of length five. Therefore \(N_G(I)\) is independent.
147	
148	The extension lemma consequently permits us to remove all small classes and restore them afterward, at a bounded cost in target size.
149	
150	Let \(W\) be the set of remaining vertices. Every support occurring in \(W\) has size at least \(2qm\).
151	
152	### A bounded triangle-free quotient of \(G[W]\)
153	
154	Refine the support partition on \(W\) by assigning \(v\in W\) the label
155	\[
156	\left(
157	 S_v,\ 
158	 \{S_u:u\in N_G(v)\cap W\}
159	\right).
160	\]
161	There are boundedly many labels. Let \(Q\) be the quotient graph: two labels are adjacent if some \(G\)-edge joins their classes.
162	
163	No class contains an edge. Indeed, if \(uv\) were an edge with \(S_u=S_v=S\), property 3 of the support lemma would say
164	\[
165	N_R(S)\cap N_R(S)=\varnothing,
166	\]
167	impossible because \(S\ne\varnothing\) and \(\delta(R)>0\).
168	
169	Thus \(G[W]\to Q\). We show that \(Q\) is triangle-free.
170	
171	Suppose three refined classes form a triangle, with supports \(S_1,S_2,S_3\), and put
172	\[
173	U_i=N_R(S_i).
174	\]
175	Property 3 gives
176	\[
177	U_1,U_2,U_3\quad\text{pairwise disjoint}. \tag{1}
178	\]
179	
180	The refinement ensures that, for every pair \(i\ne j\), there is an actual two-edge path in \(G\) whose endpoint supports are \(S_i,S_j\): choose its middle vertex in the third refined class. Property 4 therefore gives
181	\[
182	E_R(S_i,S_j)=\varnothing\qquad(i\ne j). \tag{2}
183	\]
184	Each \(S_i\) is itself independent.
185	
186	Also, the \(S_i\) are pairwise disjoint. Otherwise a vertex in \(S_i\cap S_j\) would have an \(R\)-neighbor, which would belong to \(U_i\cap U_j\), contradicting (1).
187	
188	By (2) and independence,
189	\[
190	(S_1\cup S_2\cup S_3)\cap(U_1\cup U_2\cup U_3)=\varnothing.
191	\]
192	Hence the six sets
193	\[
194	S_1,S_2,S_3,U_1,U_2,U_3
195	\]
196	are pairwise disjoint. But
197	\[
198	|S_i|\ge2qm,\qquad |U_i|\ge\delta(R)\ge qm.
199	\]
200	Consequently
201	\[
202	m\ge\sum_{i=1}^3(|S_i|+|U_i|)
203	  \ge9qm>m,
204	\]
205	a contradiction.
206	
207	So \(Q\) is triangle-free.
208	
209	There are boundedly many refined classes and boundedly many deleted small classes. Repeated use of the extension lemma produces a triangle-free target of bounded order for \(G\).
210	
211	Finally, a single target independent of \(G\) is obtained by taking the disjoint union of all triangle-free graphs up to that order. Include also all triangle-free graphs on fewer than \(n_0\) vertices to handle the finitely many small orders.
212	
213	This proves the required property for every \(c>1/9\).
214	
215	## 4. Geometric graphs for the lower bound
216	
217	We need the following finite construction.
218	
219	### Geometric lemma
220	
221	For every integer \(t\) and every \(a<1/2\), there are a finite graph \(F\), an integer \(M\), and sets
222	\[
223	A_v\subseteq[M]\qquad(v\in V(F))
224	\]
225	such that:
226	
227	1. \(\chi(F)>t\);
228	2. \(F\) contains neither \(C_3\) nor \(C_5\);
229	3. \(|A_v|\ge aM\) for every \(v\);
230	4. if a three-edge walk in \(F\) has endpoints \(u,v\), then
231	   \[
232	   A_u\cap A_v=\varnothing.
233	   \]
234	
235	**Proof.** Work on a sphere \(S^d\), where \(d\ge\max(1,t)\).
236	
237	Choose sufficiently small \(\eta>0\), with \(5\eta<2\), and set \(\alpha=2\eta\). We may make \(\eta\) so small that a uniform random point \(y\in S^d\) satisfies
238	\[
239	\Pr(\langle x,y\rangle>\alpha)>a
240	\]
241	for every unit vector \(x\). This probability is independent of \(x\) and tends to \(1/2\) as \(\alpha\downarrow0\).
242	
243	Take a finite \(\eta/4\)-net \(P\subseteq S^d\), and define
244	\[
245	pq\in E(F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \|p+q\|<\eta.
246	\]
247	
248	We first check its chromatic number. If \(F\) had a \(t\)-coloring, the unions of the open \(\eta/3\)-balls around each color class would cover \(S^d\), and no such union could contain an antipodal pair. Indeed, such a pair would yield same-colored \(p,q\) with
249	\[
250	\|p+q\|<2\eta/3<\eta.
251	\]
252	This contradicts the Borsuk–Ulam covering theorem: \(S^d\) cannot be covered by at most \(d+1\) open sets, none containing an antipodal pair.
253	
254	For completeness, that covering formulation follows from Borsuk–Ulam by taking a partition of unity \((\phi_i)\) subordinate to the cover and applying it to the odd map
255	\[
256	x\longmapsto(\phi_i(x)-\phi_i(-x))_i,
257	\]
258	whose values lie in the hyperplane with coordinate sum zero.
259	
260	For any odd walk \(p_0,\ldots,p_\ell\) in \(F\), the triangle inequality gives
261	\[
262	\|p_0+p_\ell\|<\ell\eta.
263	\]
264	An odd closed walk of length three or five would therefore give \(2<5\eta\). Thus \(F\) has neither forbidden cycle.
265	
266	Choose sufficiently many directions \(y_1,\ldots,y_M\in S^d\) so that, simultaneously for every \(p\in P\),
267	\[
268	\bigl|\{j:\langle p,y_j\rangle>\alpha\}\bigr|\ge aM.
269	\]
270	Such a finite choice exists by independent sampling and the law of large numbers, since \(P\) is finite. Define
271	\[
272	A_p=\{j:\langle p,y_j\rangle>\alpha\}.
273	\]
274	
275	If a three-edge walk joins \(p\) to \(q\), then \(\|p+q\|<3\eta\). A direction belonging to both associated sets would give
276	\[
277	3\eta>\|p+q\|
278	 \ge\langle p+q,y_j\rangle
279	 >2\alpha=4\eta,
280	\]
281	a contradiction. ∎
282	
283	## 5. Lower bound: no \(c<1/9\) works
284	
285	Fix \(c<1/9\) and an arbitrary finite triangle-free graph \(H\). Put \(h=|V(H)|\).
286	
287	Choose \(a<1/2\), sufficiently close to \(1/2\), that
288	\[
289	c<\frac{a}{3(1+a)}.
290	\]
291	Apply the geometric lemma with \(t=h\).
292	
293	Construct \(G\) as follows.
294	
295	### The core
296	
297	For every \(v\in V(F)\), make three vertices
298	\[
299	(v,0),(v,1),(v,2).
300	\]
301	Join \((u,i)\) to \((v,j)\) exactly when
302	\[
303	uv\in E(F),\qquad i\ne j.
304	\]
305	
306	### The reservoirs
307	
308	For each \(i\in\{0,1,2\}\), take:
309	
310	* an independent set \(Y_i=\{y_{i,1},\ldots,y_{i,M}\}\);
311	* an independent set \(Z_i\) of size \(L=\lfloor aM\rfloor\).
312	
313	Put all edges between \(Y_i\) and \(Z_i\). Join \((v,i)\) to \(y_{i,j}\) exactly when \(j\in A_v\). There are no other edges.
314	
315	We may replicate all reservoir directions as many times as desired before choosing \(L\).
316	
317	### Minimum degree
318	
319	Every core vertex has at least \(aM\) neighbors in its reservoir; every \(Y_i\)-vertex has at least \(L\) neighbors; every \(Z_i\)-vertex has \(M\) neighbors. Hence
320	\[
321	\delta(G)\ge L.
322	\]
323	Also
324	\[
325	|V(G)|=3|V(F)|+3M+3L.
326	\]
327	Under reservoir replication,
328	\[
329	\frac{\delta(G)}{|V(G)|}
330	 \ \ge\
331	\frac{\lfloor aM\rfloor}
332	 {3|V(F)|+3M+3\lfloor aM\rfloor}
333	 \longrightarrow \frac{a}{3(1+a)}>c.
334	\]
335	Thus a sufficiently large finite choice has \(\delta(G)\ge c|V(G)|\).
336	
337	### No triangles or pentagons
338	
339	A forbidden cycle entirely in the core would project to an odd closed walk of length three or five in \(F\), which is impossible.
340	
341	A triangle using a reservoir vertex is also impossible.
342	
343	For a \(C_5\):
344	
345	* If it contains a vertex of \(Z_i\), its two neighbors lie in \(Y_i\). A three-edge path between those neighbors, avoiding that \(Z_i\)-vertex, would require an edge between two core vertices having the same second coordinate \(i\), which does not exist.
346	* If it contains exactly one \(Y\)-vertex and no \(Z\)-vertex, the other four vertices form a three-edge core path whose endpoints have the same second coordinate and have a common reservoir neighbor. Its projection contradicts property 4 of the geometric lemma.
347	* If it contains two \(Y\)-vertices and no \(Z\)-vertex, their common intervening core vertex forces their indices to agree. The remaining two core vertices then also have that same index and would have to be adjacent, impossible.
348	
349	These exhaust the possibilities. So \(G\) is \(\{C_3,C_5\}\)-free.
350	
351	### Why \(G\) cannot map to \(H\)
352	
353	Define \(H^{[3]}\) to have an edge between vertices joined by a three-edge walk in \(H\). Since \(H\) is triangle-free, \(H^{[3]}\) has no loops.
354	
355	For every \(uv\in E(F)\), the core contains the walk
356	\[
357	(u,0),(v,1),(u,2),(v,0).
358	\]
359	Therefore a homomorphism \(G\to H\) would induce a homomorphism
360	\[
361	F\longrightarrow H^{[3]}.
362	\]
363	But \(H^{[3]}\) is a loopless graph on \(h\) vertices, whereas
364	\[
365	\chi(F)>h.
366	\]
367	This is impossible.
368	
369	As \(H\) was arbitrary, no finite triangle-free target works for \(c<1/9\).
370	
371	Combining the two halves proves the claimed infimum.
372	
373	## 6. Python verification
374	
375	The infinite assertions above are established by the proof, not by numerical experiments. The following program nevertheless checks substantive finite instances and proof components:
376	
377	* constructs an exact rational geometric example;
378	* checks all required geometric inequalities using `Fraction`;
379	* verifies the three-walk/disjoint-cap condition;
380	* constructs and checks a weighted finite lower-bound example;
381	* checks absence of \(C_3,C_5\) without relying on induced-cycle routines;
382	* checks the upper-bound set argument on every graph of order at most seven, and its nine-vertex equality configuration;
383	* checks the triangle-free extension operation on all triangle-free targets of order at most five.
384	
385	Floating point is used only to propose rational circle points; every property subsequently used is checked exactly.
386	
387	```python
388	from fractions import Fraction as Q
389	import math
390	import itertools
391	import networkx as nx
392	
393	
394	def rational_circle_point(theta, precision=10**7):
395	    # Rational stereographic parametrization.
396	    if abs(math.cos(theta / 2)) < 1e-10:
397	        return (Q(-1), Q(0))
398	    t = Q(round(math.tan(theta / 2) * precision), precision)
399	    return ((1-t*t)/(1+t*t), 2*t/(1+t*t))
400	
401	
402	def dot(x, y):
403	    return sum(a*b for a, b in zip(x, y))
404	
405	
406	def no_C3_C5(adj):
407	    # In a C3,C5-free graph, each distance-one and distance-two
408	    # neighborhood is independent; the converse also holds.
409	    n = len(adj)
410	    masks = [sum(1 << j for j in a) for a in adj]
411	    for v in range(n):
412	        one = masks[v]
413	        two = 0
414	        for u in adj[v]:
415	            two |= masks[u]
416	        two &= ~(1 << v)
417	        for S in (one, two):
418	            T = S
419	            while T:
420	                b = T & -T
421	                u = b.bit_length() - 1
422	                if masks[u] & S:
423	                    return False
424	                T -= b
425	    return True
426	
427	
428	def example(q=31, multiplicity=100):
429	    assert q % 2 == 1 and q >= 17
430	    points = [
431	        rational_circle_point(2*math.pi*j/q)
432	        for j in range(q)
433	    ]
434	    assert all(dot(p, p) == 1 for p in points)
435	
436	    step = (q-1)//2
437	    edges = {
438	        tuple(sorted((j, (j+step) % q)))
439	        for j in range(q)
440	    }
441	    F = nx.Graph()
442	    F.add_nodes_from(range(q))
443	    F.add_edges_from(edges)
444	    assert nx.is_connected(F)
445	    assert all(d == 2 for _, d in F.degree())
446	    assert not nx.is_bipartite(F)  # This F has chromatic number 3.
447	
448	    eta2 = max(
449	        2 + 2*dot(points[u], points[v])
450	        for u, v in edges
451	    )
452	    alpha = Q(4, 25)
453	    assert 25*eta2 < 4             # 5 eta < 2
454	    assert 9*eta2 < 4*alpha*alpha  # 3 eta < 2 alpha
455	
456	    caps = [
457	        {j for j, y in enumerate(points) if dot(x, y) > alpha}
458	        for x in points
459	    ]
460	    r = min(map(len, caps))
461	    assert r > 0
462	
463	    for x in F:
464	        for a in F[x]:
465	            for b in F[a]:
466	                for z in F[b]:
467	                    assert caps[x].isdisjoint(caps[z])
468	
469	    # Weighted template; independent blow-ups give actual graphs.
470	    labels = [
471	        ('X', i, x) for i in range(3) for x in range(q)
472	    ]
473	    labels += [
474	        ('Y', i, j) for i in range(3) for j in range(q)
475	    ]

305	
306	For each \(i\in\{0,1,2\}\), take:

309	* an independent set \(Z_i\) of size \(L=\lfloor aM\rfloor\).

311	Put all edges between \(Y_i\) and \(Z_i\). Join \((v,i)\) to \(y_{i,j}\) exactly when \(j\in A_v\). There are no other edges.

313	We may replicate all reservoir directions as many times as desired before choosing \(L\).

315	### Minimum degree
316	
317	Every core vertex has at least \(aM\) neighbors in its reservoir; every \(Y_i\)-vertex has at least \(L\) neighbors; every \(Z_i\)-vertex has \(M\) neighbors. Hence
318	\[
319	\delta(G)\ge L.
320	\]

322	\[
323	|V(G)|=3|V(F)|+3M+3L.
324	\]

326	\[
327	\frac{\delta(G)}{|V(G)|}
328	 \ \ge\
329	\frac{\lfloor aM\rfloor}

331	 \longrightarrow \frac{a}{3(1+a)}>c.
